cards.answer: Braum is a tank support who intercepts projectiles and helps allies stun enemies. He can leap to an ally and temporarily give both of them armor and magic resistance.
cards.counterplay: Avoid letting Braum and his allies repeatedly attack you after he applies a stack. Attack from outside his shield's facing direction.

citations.quote: Name: Braum. Official role tags: Tank, Support.
Braum raises his shield in a direction for several seconds, intercepting all projectiles causing them to hit him and be destroyed.
Once the first stack is applied, ally basic attacks also stack Concussive Blows. Upon reaching 4 stacks, the target is stunned and takes magic damage.

facts.claim: intercepts projectiles and helps allies stun enemies

citations.quote: Braum leaps to a target allied champion or minion. On arrival, Braum and the ally gain Armor and Magic Resist for a few seconds.

facts.claim: He can leap to an ally and temporarily give both of them armor and magic resistance.

cards.priority_reason: Understanding his protection and allied stun setup explains his fighting role.
uncertainties: Build focus is a broad learning recommendation grounded in tank role, defensive resistances and Q's maximum-health scaling, not an item build.

cards.answer: Braum's basic attacks apply Concussive Blows stacks; after the first stack, allied champions' basic attacks also add stacks. At 4 stacks, the target is stunned and takes magic damage. Afterward, the target temporarily cannot gain new stacks, but Braum's basic attacks deal bonus magic damage to it.
cards.counterplay: Back away from Braum and his allies when stacks begin building on you.

citations.quote: Braum's basic attacks apply Concussive Blows. Once the first stack is applied, ally basic attacks also stack Concussive Blows.
Once the first stack has been applied, any allied champion's basic attack applies an additional stack to the target on-hit.

citations.quote: Upon reaching 4 stacks, the target is stunned and takes magic damage.

facts.claim: At 4 stacks, the target is stunned and takes magic damage.

passive_visual.description: A stack marker builds beneath the target, then disappears when the stun triggers.

cards.priority_reason: Allied basic attacks can quickly turn an initial stack into a stun.
uncertainties: Visual cue is a tentative proposal based on the supplied official-clip frames, not current-client or skin-specific verification; riot:P identifies the associated passive.
Stacks expire and refresh on subsequent applications; dodged, blocked or missed attacks do not apply them. These advanced details are omitted from the beginner explanation.

cards.answer: Braum fires ice in a chosen direction, dealing magic damage to and slowing the first enemy hit. It also applies a Concussive Blows stack.
cards.counterplay: Dodge the ice projectile to avoid its slow and passive stack.

citations.quote: Applies a stack of Concussive Blows.
Braum's basic attacks and Winter's Bite apply a stack of Concussive Blows.

facts.claim: It also applies a Concussive Blows stack.

cards.priority_reason: The ranged slow and initial passive stack help set up allied follow-up attacks.

cards.answer: Braum leaps to a targeted allied champion or minion. On arrival, he and that ally temporarily gain armor and magic resistance.
cards.counterplay: Account for Braum leaping to a nearby ally when choosing a target. Avoid committing damage into their temporary resistance boost when possible.

cards.answer: Braum raises a directional shield that intercepts incoming hostile projectiles it can block, making them hit him and be destroyed. From that direction, he fully negates the first eligible instance of champion damage and reduces subsequent eligible damage while the shield is raised.
cards.counterplay: Attack from another direction to avoid his directional protection. Do not rely on a projectile passing through him to reach an ally.

citations.quote: Braum raises his shield in a direction for several seconds, intercepting all projectiles causing them to hit him and be destroyed.
creating a barrier in front of him that intercepts all incoming hostile projectiles
Projectiles that cannot hit Braum or his allies (such as an enemy Prismatic Barrier) will not be intercepted.[2]

facts.claim: Braum raises a directional shield that intercepts incoming hostile projectiles it can block, making them hit him and be destroyed.

citations.quote: The first instance of damage dealt by a champion from this direction is reduced by 100%.
reduces the damage Braum takes through it from enemies in the target direction.
He negates the damage of the first attack completely and reduces the damage of all subsequent attacks from this direction.

facts.claim: From that direction, he fully negates the first eligible instance of champion damage and reduces subsequent eligible damage while the shield is raised.

cards.priority_reason: Projectile interception and directional damage denial can disrupt attacks aimed at his team.
uncertainties: Eligible damage excludes an assumption of true-damage negation; the source only establishes that pure true damage does not consume the first-hit reduction.
Turrets are unaffected. Damage reduction benefits only Braum and can apply beyond projectiles.
Intercepted projectiles can still trigger collision effects, debuffs and areas that affect other units.
Simultaneous damage, damage-over-time ticks, airborne summoned units, Rejuvenation and spell shields have advanced interaction rules omitted here.

cards.answer: Braum slams the ground, dealing magic damage and knocking up enemies around him and along a line in front of him. The fissure leaves a lingering ice field that slows enemies within it.
cards.counterplay: Move out of the line in front of Braum and avoid lingering in the ice field.

citations.quote: Braum slams the ground, knocking up enemies nearby and in a line in front of him.
creating a fissure from the impact that travels forth in the target direction, dealing magic damage to enemies within its path as well as those around Braum.

facts.claim: Braum slams the ground, dealing magic damage and knocking up enemies around him and along a line in front of him.

citations.quote: A fissure is left along the line that slows enemies.
A field of ice is created along the fissure's path, lasting for 4 seconds and slowing enemies within the area every 0.25 seconds.

facts.claim: The fissure leaves a lingering ice field that slows enemies within it.

cards.priority_reason: The knockup and lingering slow can disrupt several enemies and control their movement.
uncertainties: The first target's knockup duration increases with distance; other targets receive a shorter fixed knockup. Exact durations are omitted.

conflicts.resolution: Use eligible hostile projectiles and eligible champion damage to preserve the core behavior without implying universal interception or true-damage negation. Retain detailed exceptions in QA metadata.
conflicts.topic: Riot's broad projectile and first-attack wording is qualified by Wiki's eligibility, champion-damage and interaction details.

cooldown_candidates.reason: Shield availability determines whether Braum can intercept projectiles and deny incoming damage.
Ultimate availability changes the threat of a line knockup and lingering slow field.
Leap availability affects his ability to reach an ally and grant resistances.
Projectile availability affects his ranged slow and passive-stack setup.
